notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text is a full 31-page research manuscript, with matching title Double misinformation: Effects on eyewitness remembering and all six reference authors (Hartmut Blank, Anu Panday, Ross Edwards, Ewa Skopicz-Radkiewicz, Violet Gibson, Vasudevi Reddy). It includes methods, results, references, tables and figure, and is a primary report rather than an abstract, secondary report or preregistration. SOURCE_URL identifies the University of Portsmouth manuscript Double_misinformation_paper_14.pdf. DOI and journal publication metadata are not printed in this text, so exact published-version identity is not independently established. No local PDF is supplied; no rendering or acquisition performed. The outcome identifies accuracy but does not distinguish the simple correlation from the partial correlation controlling original-detail availability. The p. 16 locator gives pooled Figure 1 analyses across experiments, whereas study_o is 1. No basis is supplied to resolve pooled versus Experiment 1 scope or simple versus partial test. No target assigned by row order or numeric matching. Page 16 candidates: simple Pearson r = -.70, p < .001, one-tailed; partial r = -.69, p < .01 (the sentence does not separately state its sidedness). Both are printed coefficients; no conversion. Additional study-scope candidates: Table 4, p. 29, Experiment 1 correlations -.80 (recognition) and -.94 (cued recall), without row-specific p values; aggregate across experiments -.86, p = .033 (one-tailed p printed on p. 15). These are distinct tests and are not merged. Analytic N candidate only: p. 14 footnote 6 explicitly states 18 black data points in Figure 1 for the pooled endorsement analysis, and refers to corresponding white accuracy points. These are item-by-experiment/test observations, not participants; no N inferred from df. The same graph is cited for p. 16 simple and partial analyses, but unresolved target scope prevents assigning 18 to this row. For Experiment 1, pp. 10–11 describe three critical items in each of recognition and cued recall; these imply separate three-item correlation sets, not 42 participant observations. Participant contributor counts on p. 8 are 42, 60, 96 for Experiments 1–3 and are not assigned as analytic N. Page 12 states no outliers removed and all relevant data points used. No mutually exclusive final-group N sum is used. Unassigned replication and reported_success fields are placeholders only. Original status done means source inspection completed; target_match remains null and numeric fields null because correspondence is unresolved.
